transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-26
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chang (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morris (CISO, Crestmont), Tom Reeves (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security posture intake focused on whether Crestmont can use Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO artifacts and scope, customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM/KMS), SSO/SAML integration and SCIM provisioning, RBAC granularity and audit logs retention, regional data residency, and backup/encrypted snapshots.

Topics covered:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 type II, ISO27001) and scope (production, backups, logs)
- Key management options (RKM / BYOK / HSM integration) and key rotation
- SSO/SAML, SCIM, provisioning, RBAC roles and admin separation
- Audit logs, redaction, retention, and access for auditors
- Deployment models: Hosted API tradeoffs vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem
- Network controls: VPC peering, private control plane, egress restrictions

Action items (brief): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. real quick i'll run through agenda, intro jordan from our se team, and then we'll dive into security + deployment questions.
[00:23] Elena (Crestmont CISO): thanks, and uh yeah we mostly want to understand how you handle customer keys, what the soc two cover, and how logs are handled. also where data lives.
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood SE): great. quick note: we support hosted, dedicated, and private. hosted is the fastest, dedi is reserved capacity but shared control plane, private gives you a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. for keys we have two main paths: customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and redwood-managed keys. you can also integrate with an HSM for additional attestations.
[01:05] Tom (Platform Eng): when you say BYOK, do you support key wrapping via external HSM? like we need to have key custody in our Cloud HSM and Redwood shouldn't be able to decrypt without the wrapped key.
[01:20] Jordan (SE): yes, we support KMS integration across major clouds — you can bring your own key and we only receive a wrapped key. for private deployments we can also integrate with customer HSMs over established tunnels. there's a doc i'll share with sample flow diagrams. (mumbles) the integration uses envelope encryption, and keys never stored in plaintext on the service.
[01:52] Priya (Compliance): okay, and rotation? we have quarterly rotation requirements and a key history for audits.
[02:02] Jordan: rotation is supported — you can rotate in KMS and the runtime handles new key epochs; we also keep a rotation log for auditing. note: for hosted, we rely on cloud KMS APIs, for private deployments rotations happen under your control.
[02:25] Elena: moving to SOC2/ISO, do you have SOC2 type II? what's in scope — is logs and backups included?
[02:35] Avery: yes we have SOC2 Type II, and ISO27001 certificates. i'll send the artifacts, but scope varies by offering; hosted includes platform, control plane, and data at rest, but if you need contract-level guarantees for backups and archival, we can show the scope in the report. some customers request dedicated scoping for private deployments.
[02:58] Tom: are audit logs available for export to our SIEM? we need raw logs for at least 2 years for some regulators.
[03:10] Jordan: audit logs can be streamed to customer S3 or equivalent via secure transfer for dedicated/private. hosted offers log exports too but retention windows differ. for very long retention we recommend routing logs to your account. note there is a small egress cost if we push logs out.
[03:40] Priya: retention windows — baseline hosted retention is 90 days? can you do 2 years?
[03:49] Avery: yep baseline is 90 for hosted, but for enterprise customers we offer extended retention as an add-on or via dedicated/private where logs live in your tenancy and you can set retention to meet policy, e.g., 2 years.
[04:10] Elena: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles: admin separation, developer, auditor read-only, and service accounts. also need SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning to sync groups.
[04:25] Jordan: we have RBAC with predefined roles and ability to define custom roles in private. SAML SSO is supported; SCIM provisioning is available for enterprise plans — we can auto-provision groups. for hosted we recommend scoped service tokens and secrets management.
[04:48] Tom: does RBAC control extend to model rollouts and who can change routing policies? we need separation so ops can manage capacity but product team can't change key access.
[04:59] Jordan: yes those are separate permission domains — model config and routing vs key management. in private, you have full control over RBAC mappings to your LDAP/IdP.
[05:20] Elena: another regulatory ask: data residency in EU region. our data processing must stay in EU data centers and we cannot have cross-border replication unless contractually permitted. can you guarantee that?
[05:34] Avery: we offer region pinning for hosted and dedicated. private gives the most control since control plane also lives in your VPC/region. for hosted we can pin to eu-west1, but note some artifacts like audit logs backups might transit — we can add contractual SLAs in DPA.
[05:58] Tom: backups — are snapshots encrypted with a separate key, and who decrypts for restores?
[06:06] Jordan: snapshots are encrypted at rest; for BYOK we encrypt snapshots with your KMS keys. restores require the key in your KMS; Redwood cannot decrypt if BYOK is used and key is never exported. for redwood-managed keys we manage decrypt operations for restore under our controls.
[06:30] Priya: legal will want an incident runbook and evidence of playbooks, time to detection/mttr numbers. do you have that?
[06:41] Avery: yes we have an IR playbook and we capture detection and response metrics — i'll include the IR summary in the artifacts link. we have pager duty hooks and can agree on notif cadence in SLA.
[06:54] Elena: about encryption in transit — we need mTLS between our services and the Redwood private control plane for private deployment.
[07:04] Jordan: mTLS is supported for the private control plane endpoints; for hosted/dedicated we rely on TLS mutual auth for sensitive flows and tokens for API. we can do client cert pinning for additional safety.
[07:22] Tom: auditability for model outputs — can you redact PII before storing logs? some of our logs will contain customer identifiers.
[07:33] Jordan: we offer configurable redaction hooks. you can opt to not persist request/response bodies, or redact sensitive fields via pre-store transforms. we recommend a combination of prefix caching and redaction rules for PII heavy workloads.
[07:55] Elena: do you provide attestation for supply chain, SBOMs for runtime libs, and vulnerability scanning for your runtime images?
[08:04] Avery: yes we publish SBOMs and perform regular scans; for private we can provide image signing and attestations that match your CI. i'll drop the SBOM link.
[08:18] Tom: network controls — can we enforce egress rules and restrict outbound calls from the runtime? we want to limit any call to external endpoints except allowed whitelisted sinks.
[08:28] Jordan: on private you control egress through your VPC egress gateways; on dedicated we have policies to restrict egress to whitelisted endpoints and telemetry sinks. hosted is more restricted but we offer per-tenant egress controls for enterprise.
[08:45] Priya: what's the retention policy for KV cache — are those considered logs or ephemeral caches? some regulators treat cached contexts as data subject records.
[08:56] Jordan: KV cache is ephemeral by default and stored encrypted in memory; we can configure persistence windows. for regulated workloads we recommend zero-persistence mode or short TTLs and storing keys/indices in your tenancy.
[09:18] Elena: do you run penetration tests and can we get the summary?
[09:24] Avery: we do yearly pentests and can provide a summary of findings and mitigation steps — not the full report, but an executive summary suitable for customers.
[09:35] Tom: SSO specifics — do you support multiple IdPs for different org units? we have subsidiaries that use different providers.
[09:44] Jordan: we support multiple IdPs on the same account and mapping to SCIM groups. there's a little provisioning complexity, but we have a runbook.
[09:58] Priya: about attestations and audits — if we go private, will Redwood allow auditor access to logs/traces for our auditors?
[10:08] Avery: in private, since logs live in your account/tenancy, you can grant auditors access directly. for dedicated we can set up read-only auditor roles. for hosted we can provide tailored extracts and SOC2 evidence.
[10:25] Elena: threat model question — how do you separate tenants at the runtime level? any noisy neighbor protections?
[10:34] Jordan: separation at compute level with per-tenant TLS certs, process sandboxing, and dedicated GPU queues for dedicated customers. we also do kernel hardening and cgroups. noisy neighbor mitigations include preemption policies and quota enforcement.
[10:58] Tom: ok curious about model updates — if you push a model update, how do you handle compatibility and can we opt out?
[11:08] Jordan: you can pin model versions per route. we provide canary rollouts and A/B routing. updates are opt-in unless in critical security patches.
[11:22] Elena: what about data exfil detection? do you monitor for anomalous prompt patterns or outbound tokens that match PII?
[11:33] Jordan: we have anomaly detection on usage patterns and token leakage heuristics. you can also route logs to your SIEM and run custom detection rules.
[11:50] Tom: performance benchmarking — we need to run a POC with secure data and measure 95th p99 latency for multi-turn chat. can we do this on dedicated or private?
[12:02] Avery: dedicated is typically used for predictable perf; private gives you the most control. we can run a bench on dedicated for the first pass, then move to private for final validation. Jordan will draft a plan.
[12:20] Jordan: i'll build a bench that measures p50/p95/p99, throughput under batching, and KV-cache hit rates. we'll include a sample CSV for you to run tests.
[12:33] Priya: legal will want DPA and data processing terms with EU data residency clauses.
[12:40] Avery: understood; i'll include a sample DPA and DPA addendum for EU residency.
[12:48] Elena: one more — audit trails for admin actions, like who rotated a key or changed RBAC. are those immutable auditable events?
[12:58] Jordan: yes we produce tamper-evident audit logs with hashes and chain-of-custody metadata; for private those logs are stored in your storage and can be WORM if required.
[13:16] Tom: any limitations with SAML providers? our IdP uses certificate rollover frequently.
[13:23] Jordan: we support metadata refresh and certificate rollover — SCIM handles mapping, and we have test harness for rotation.
[13:36] Elena: ok given all that, high-level tradeoffs for us: Hosted = fast but less control; Dedicated = predictable throughput + better controls; Private = max control for regs but longer lead time. is that right?
[13:50] Avery: that's correct. also cost delta — private has infra and ops overhead; dedicated is middle ground. we'll include cost comparisons in the follow-up.
[14:05] Tom: can you point to any finance customers who've run private for KYC/AML workloads? we want references on the governance model.
[14:14] Avery: we can share anonymized reference list and case studies — i'll include contacts where permitted.
[14:24] Priya: what about support SLAs during incident windows? we need 24/7 for priority incidents.
[14:31] Avery: enterprise plans include 24/7 on-call and priority SLAs; dedicated/private can have tighter MTTR targets as part of contract.
[14:45] Jordan: quick callout about token logging: by default we log token metadata and not full prompt bodies; storing full prompts is configurable. be mindful of regulatory requirements if you store user-provided PII.
[15:03] Tom: will the bench tests require us to share sample data? we prefer redacted/obf versions.
[15:09] Jordan: that's fine — we can run with synthetic or redacted sets. for accurate latency under real-world prompts we suggest a small redacted corpus.
[15:25] Elena: ok let's talk timeline — we're hoping to make a vendor decision by end of Q2. we need to run a POC in April/May.
[15:36] Avery: that's doable. proposed timeline: artifacts out this week, bench plan early March, POC in April, legal review in parallel.
[15:46] Tom: any blockers for on-prem private? what's typical lead time?
[15:52] Jordan: private on-prem lead time varies — typically 6 to 10 weeks for deployment and network setup depending on approvals. dedicated is faster, 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity. hosted is immediate.
[16:10] Priya: one compliance nuance: cross-border backups to US are prohibited without binding clauses. can we ensure backups stay in-region?
[16:19] Avery: yes for private/dedicated we can confine backups to region and add contractual clauses in the DPA. for hosted we can pin region and set no cross-border replication policy as part of the contract.
[16:35] Elena: curious about logging access controls — who at Redwood can see logs in hosted? is there separation and SSO access?
[16:45] Jordan: internal access is tightly controlled with RBAC, approval workflows, and just-in-time elevation. we also maintain access logs for internal ops and can supply redacted extracts for audits.
[16:58] Tom: data deletion — if we terminate service, what's the deletion process and certificates to confirm deletion?
[17:06] Avery: we have a data deletion workflow and can provide deletion certificates. for BYOK customers, keys are invalidated and data becomes unrecoverable. we'll include the deletion SLA in the DPA.
[17:22] Priya: any specific certifications around privacy like ISO/IEC 27701?
[17:28] Avery: we have ISO27001 and are working on 27701 in certain offerings — i'll confirm the status in the follow up.
[17:40] Elena: ok last question — do you offer MSSP integrations for managed monitoring?
[17:46] Jordan: yes we have partners for managed detection and response and can forward integration guides.
[17:56] Avery: great, looks like we've captured the main concerns. jordan, will you outline the bench and security tech deep dive?
[18:03] Jordan: yep i'll send a bench plan and a private deployment network checklist.
[18:12] Priya: legal will want to vet the SOC2 scope and DPA before we sign anything.
[18:18] Avery: understood — will prioritize sending SOC2/ISO/ DPA samples.
[18:26] Elena: thanks. can you also include a short note on which features require dedicated vs private vs hosted? that's helpful for procurement.
[18:34] Avery: sure we'll include a features matrix in the follow-up doc.
[18:42] Tom: perfect. any final questions?
[18:45] Priya: none from me.
[18:47] Elena: none. thanks all.
